verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The Lean has the same block structure but states the vanishing at the level of the integral operators rather than as a matrix identity for an unspecified kernel. DerivativeShape (line 57) is the paper's sparse form of A_1 ('maps the first four coordinates into the last two and annihilates the last two'), holding at every radius and every parameter point, hence also after a parameter derivative. Recovery of the display for the intervening kernel actually in play, D_0 = G = radialInverse: A_1 D_0 A_1 F = matrixAction A₁ (radialInverse (matrixAction A₁ F)) = 0, by matrixAction_lowZero_eq_zero (92) applied to lowZero_radialInverse (81) applied to lowZero_matrixAction (64); the second identity inserts lowZero_parameterDeriv (73) in the same chain. adjacent_derivative_letters_zero (131) is the packaged consequence the paper draws in the next sentence, and its proof differentiates identically-zero components, so it covers the Leibniz term in which ∂_η falls on the adjacent coefficient. What the Lean does not state is the paper's quantification over an arbitrary diagonal kernel D_0: only radialInverse and parameterDeriv (and their composites) are covered, which are the only intervening kernels the argument uses.
